items.title: The critical distinction between base LLMs (2024 and earlier) and modern LRMs is not symbolic tool u...
items.content:
The critical distinction between base LLMs (2024 and earlier) and modern LRMs is not symbolic tool use. It's the switch from a transductive paradigm (intuit the answer to the query) to an inductive paradigm (intuit the program/instructions that produce the answer to the query).

They're trained to be inductive, and they perform test-time induction, i.e. test-time prediction of a NL program / reasoning chain. This unlocks entirely new capabilities -- in particular fluid intelligence. Base LLMs, to this day, have ~0 fluid intelligence. LRMs have substantial levels of fluid intelligence.

The performance of LLMs on ARC 1 (a benchmark from 2019) remains ~10-15% today. Scaling them up by a factor ~100,000x got them from 0% to 10%. Meanwhile LRMs the same size or smaller saturated ARC 1 in 2025.

He supports this with ARC data: base LLMs remain at ~10-15% on ARC 1 despite ~100,000x scaling, while same-size-or-smaller LRMs saturated it in 2025.

items.content:
Mods are absolutely insane. You can now customize Claude to work and look the way you want by just prompting it.

Each person works differently, so there's no reason why everyone should have an identical Claude experience. Make Claude your own, and share mods as plugins so others can try your mods too.

items.title: Microsoft AI has released MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, taking the #1 spot for Final Transcript accura...
items.content:
Microsoft AI has released MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, taking the #1 spot for Final Transcript accuracy and First Partial Transcript accuracy on AA-WER Streaming with 2.5% WER at 0.13s after end of speech

MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming is @MicrosoftAI's new streaming Speech to Text model, joining the non-streaming MAI-Transcribe-2. It leads streaming Final Transcript WER at 2.5%, ahead of the previous #1, SpaceXAI's Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 at 2.7%, and returns that transcript in 0.13s rather than 0.49s. It is available for streaming transcription at $0.54 per hour of audio, at the higher end of pricing among the leading streaming models.

Key takeaways

➤ Final Transcript: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming achieves 2.5% WER at 0.13s after end of speech, ranking #1 of 38 models. It is more accurate and faster than Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 at 2.7% and 0.49s, Muse Voice Transcribe at 3.1% and 0.16s, and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime at 3.6% and 0.14s. It is also more accurate, though slightly slower, than Cartesia Ink Preview (external endpoints) at 3.1% and 0.11s

➤ First Partial Transcript: The model achieves 2.5% WER at 0.12s, ahead of Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 at 3.4% and 0.49s, and ahead of Muse Voice Transcribe and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime on accuracy, both at 3.6%, and slightly faster than both at 0.12s versus 0.13s. It is more accurate but slower than Cartesia Ink-2 (external endpoints) at 4.0% and 0.07s

➤ Price: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming costs $0.54 per hour for streaming, or $9.00 per 1,000 minutes. This puts it level with Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live at $9, above the $6.50 charged for ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime and Deepgram Flux, more than twice Cartesia Ink-2 at $4, and three times Muse Voice Transcribe at $3. Non-streaming transcription costs $0.10 per hour, or $1.67 per 1,000 minutes

Congrats to the @MicrosoftAI team on the launch!

@Dan_Jeffries1 Question for everyone :
Are you pro-intelligence or anti-intelligence ? 
Do you think more intelligence in the world is intrinsically good ? 
Or do you think more intelligence is intrinsically dangerous ? 

AI amplifies human intelligence.
It makes PEOPLE smarter and more effective.
It's like search engines, libraries, education, literacy, language: it makes PEOPLE smarter and more empowered. 

If you want intelligence (artificial or natural) to be under control of a few companies or governments, you are a neo-obscurantist or a neo-feudalist.

T...
items.content:
Today we’re introducing Extract v2.5 - a series of frontier agents tuned for document extraction.

The agents (cost-effective, agentic, agentic plus) are tuned for value accuracy and grounding. Our extraction agents outperform Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol while being 30%-4x cheaper. 

We’ve made massive improvements on complex extraction over 
* long lists (86.1% -> 95.5% on our agentic tier)
* records spanning pages (85.5% -> 96.5%)
* scanned forms (90.9% -> 95.7%)

We’ve also launched the following features:
✅ Advanced citations: we locate bounding boxes for all supporting values for an inferred field, even if there's not an exact match.
✅ Structural Reasoning: we tailor document extraction algorithms depending on the type, layout, and information

Our extraction agents are SOTA in price-performance on ExtractBench, across a wide range of cost points. We are the best tool for document extraction across documents of any complexity.

Blog: https://t.co/TTlTdECU03

All of these are available on LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8 . Come check it out!

items.content:
In physics, an “impedance mismatch” occurs when two systems each work well but are poorly matched.

In this Science Blog guest post, Harvard physicist Matthew Schwartz argues that something similar is happening with AI and science. LLMs are capable at many things, but working with them as you would with a human collaborator isn’t currently the best way to elicit their scientific strengths.

To address this mismatch, Schwartz created a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science. Because similar calculations often emerge in very different areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields, and Schwartz worked with domain experts to steer it towards interesting questions.

Read more about these projects here: https://t.co/UpgSwMCz7h

Qwen-Im...
items.content:
Alibaba's Qwen-Image-2.1 is the new #1 open weights model on both the AA-Image leaderboards

Qwen-Image-2.1 is Alibaba's latest image model, released with open weights on September 20. It has a 7B parameter visual generation component and handles Text to Image and Image Editing in a single model, with native 2K output and native transparent (RGBA) image generation and editing. The weights are released under the Qwen Research License, which requires a separate license for commercial use. 

In the absence of major inference providers hosting this model at time of launch, we evaluated Qwen-Image-2.1 by hosting it locally.

Qwen-Image-2.1 ranks #18 on AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and on AA-Image-Editing v2.0, and leads all open weights models on both, ahead of Ideogram 4.0 (Quality) in Text to Image and HunyuanImage 3.0 Instruct in Image Editing. It is a large step up on Qwen Image 2.0, climbing from #72 to #18 in AA-Image-T2I v2.0 and from #58 to #18 in AA-Image-Editing v2.0.

The weights are available on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with day-0 support in Diffusers, ComfyUI, vLLM-Omni, SGLang and LightX2V.

Congratulations to @Alibaba_Qwen on the release!

See below for our analysis and example outputs of Qwen-Image-2.1 in the Artificial Analysis Image Arena 🧵

items.title: Safety refusal reporting in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index now shows when refusals occur...
items.content:
Safety refusal reporting in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index now shows when refusals occur and which models are used as fallbacks

We've added two ways to explore the results:

➤ Refusal timing: see whether a refusal occurred from the task prompt alone or later in the task, after the agent had already started working

➤ Fallback model: see which model the agent switched to after a refusal, alongside attempts that were blocked

Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 (max) currently ranks first in the Index. Its safety refusal rate is 4.5%, roughly half the 8.9% recorded for Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (max).

Around 94% of Sonnet 5.5's refusals occurred after the first turn. Following a refusal, the agent almost always switched to Opus 4.8.

Observed fallback patterns vary across model and agent configurations. With Fable 5.1, Claude Code fell back predominantly to Opus 4.8, while Opus 5 accounted for a much larger share of Devin Fusion's fallbacks in the Index.

Both views are available for the overall Index and each benchmark. Safety and fallback behavior is provider-configured and may change over time; these rates reflect behavior recorded at the time of benchmarking.

SITUATION EXPLAINED: Will the US government own a piece of OpenAI and Anthropic?

• Asked if he'd na...
items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: Will the US government own a piece of OpenAI and Anthropic?

• Asked if he'd nationalize them, Trump said no. The guardrail is the Department of Justice
• On taking a 10% stake the way he did with Intel: "I might. Maybe I could do that." He says the Intel stake has made the government about $60 billion
• OpenAI reportedly offered Washington a 5% stake back in July. Anthropic and the administration denied discussing one
• On Dario: "I spoke to him about his views, and they're much different than what is portrayed in the media. Very smart guy, maybe different than I thought a little bit"
• On rogue agents: they're not allowed to do that, and if they do, there could be penalties that are not going to be acceptable to them

@theojaffee: "Trump is not this hyper-accelerationist caricature. He's interested in liability for frontier labs or models that do bad things. He respects Dario. He's not calling Anthropic a woke radical left whatever."

It basical...
items.content:
This pareto-26.10-preview model is pretty cool. It does something I haven't seen before:

It basically combines multiple models behind one API response:

1. You send a request
2. Pareto runs several models to produce answers
3. It then evaluates the answers and selects the best
4. It returns that answer back to you

You don't need to build a comparison/selection system since it's built in when you use this model.

It's also cheap: $0.80/MTk in and $3.20/Mtk out. That's cheaper than
Sol and 10x cheaper than Fable or Astra.

items.title: Tennr CEO @TreyHolterman predicts a healthcare paradox where AI makes medical advice easier to acces...
items.content:
Tennr CEO @TreyHolterman predicts a healthcare paradox where AI makes medical advice easier to access but specialists even harder to see:

"Last time I was sick I was definitely talking to chat about it. Now, chat is a little bit trigger-happy. Just like a primary care, they're like, 'Oh, that sounds really bad. Let's get you sent out.'"

"You're gonna have these three-month wait lists to see a rheumatologist. They're gonna go to five months, because suddenly every single person is gonna feel like they really need to go into a rheumatologist because of some rash. That risks taking up the slots of patients that really do need to be seen urgently. That's the bear case."

"In the bull case, you have overburdened coordinators that can't tell the difference between a patient that's stat, high acuity, and a patient that's getting a fourth opinion because they're a little nervous from something they read on chat."

"You have to bet that the models are gonna allow them to triage the patients that really need to be seen."

items.title: Pace CEO @jamiecuffe predicts computer-use agents could take insurance from checking just 1% of clai...
items.content:
Pace CEO @jamiecuffe predicts computer-use agents could take insurance from checking just 1% of claims and underwriting decisions to checking 100% in real time:

"The lingua franca of the industry is really emails and PDFs, and that's why it's so good for agents, because there aren't these APIs to be able to do this work."

"Systems that don't have APIs, legacy web apps, desktop apps, even green screen terminals running on an IBM mainframe. Agents can log into those systems the same way a human would, spin up a virtual desktop, enter that information."

"Today, a lot of companies are quality assuring 1% of the underwriting or claims decisions that they make. If it's now an order of magnitude cheaper to do that with agents, why wouldn't you just QA 100%? And why would you do it post-fact? You can just do it always on in real time."
@pacecom

items.title: I'm sorry for scientists and software engineers who are depressed about the fact that AI is doing mo...
items.content:
I'm sorry for scientists and software engineers who are depressed about the fact that AI is doing most of work they have been doing.

I know that some found pleasure in writing code in anticipation to see it working either in production or driving an experiment, but nothing prevents anyone from keeping doing that by hand.

Some artisans still make nails manually, some restore old cars manually, if it makes you feel happy, keep doing that.

But business always switched to more effective and efficient approaches, and using AI is such a switch. No regular client will want to pay for a modern house made with artisanal nails, $10 a nail, so construction contractors use mass made nails. This doesn't make their work less exciting.

If tomorrow, a technology will be able to print a house, the construction workers will deliver whole neighborhoods with underground tunnels, nuclear bunkers, and alpine ski hills.

items.title: Nace AI just released Drex 1.5 — the first (and so far the only) decision model with a 128k context ...
items.content:
Nace AI just released Drex 1.5 — the first (and so far the only) decision model with a 128k context window.

128k is really good! You can send an entire contract or a video transcript and get a scored decision over the whole thing. You don't need to mess with chunking or stitching results back together.

The idea is the same as with Jev:

• Input: context + a set of choices
• Output: classification + score for every option

For example, you can use Drex to classify a review as "POSITIVE", "NEGATIVE", or "NEUTRAL", and route any low-scored answer to a human for further inspection.

Here is where the model differs from Jev:

• 128k context
• Small - It's under 10B parameters
• $0.04 per 1M input tokens, a bit cheaper than Jev

The model is #1 on the Decision Index 0.2.1 (chance-corrected; random guessing = 0):

 • Drex: 58.28
 • Jev 1.13.0: 57.91

Nace is giving 250M free tokens to the first 10,000 builders: https://t.co/Q2j9qu28KY

Thanks to the @NaceAI team for partnering with me on this post.

This is the dream job for anyone looking to become an automation engineer in AI:

You'll join a team, learn its processes, and build automations for their work:

1. You'll meet with the people who are doing the work
2. You'll find and connect the systems needed to complete it
3. You'll build and validate the workflows
4. You'll teach the team how to extend what you built
5. Pick a new problem, and repeat

• Full-time
• 2 years of experience
• Working knowledge of APIs and IAM
• On-site in San Francisco, New York, Austin, or Charleston
• $105,000 - $170,000/year + equity

items.title: Tennr CEO @TreyHolterman says healthcare breaks when the insurer deciding whether you get treatment ...
items.content:
Tennr CEO @TreyHolterman says healthcare breaks when the insurer deciding whether you get treatment is also financially rewarded for saying no:

"Almost any incentive that you set up can be gamed to a tremendous degree."

"More than 50% of patients have moved from Medicare to Medicare Advantage, which is basically just Medicare managed by payers. If they're fed $20 billion ahead of time, I am going to approve, approve, approve until I get to exactly what I was paid to dispense, and then I'm gonna deny, deny, deny every single thing that comes after."

"I've seen primary care networks where they're incentivized by the health of their patients. ChenMed in Florida is doing this to an incredible degree. They do not make more money the more treatments a patient gets."

"Primary care has been made to be this gatekeeper that has to spend five minutes per patient. If we can fund primary care a lot more effectively, a lot more of that responsibility comes to a provider that's actually interested in the patient, not to a payer."

items.title: This is how winning companies fail. Two years ago, when I started vibe coding, I was recommended by ...
items.content:
This is how winning companies fail. Two years ago, when I started vibe coding, I was recommended by the AI to use @supabase as the backend and it made sense: it's a Postgres-based database (so no hard vendor lock-in) and Deno-based edge functions (again no lock-in).

During these two years, I found several limitations that made me use GCP more often than I would like to.

One limitation is that edge functions can live only up to 150 seconds. The declared limit of 400 seconds is hardly achievable in practice due to other limitations.

150 seconds is obviously an arbitrary number they chose many years ago. With today's hardware, this could easily be extended to several minutes, maybe up to an hour. But they haven't done anything.

The second limitation is that the edge function cannot import any of the npm libraries. Pure JS/TS only. Really?

The third limitation, and this one is really like WTF, is that a harness cannot pull logs of failed edge functions using the CLI. Until this year, I used to go to the console myself, copy the log, and paste it into the harness. Now the harness opens the browser and uses the UI to get the logs.

What the fucking fuck?

I'm furious for one only reason: How can you be in this domain, be somewhat a leader with a brand well known in the industry, and not fucking strive to be a leader? Many would give anything to be in your position, but you got lucky and what do you do with your incredible luck? Drain it down the toilet.

items.content:
Pretty clever: a model routing and quality-control layer, but for voice models.

Basically, @OnepinAI sits on top of existing TTS providers.

• It normalizes the script
• It selects a voice model for different lines
• It generates the voiceover
• It checks pronunciation, clarity, and naturalness
• It fixes or regenerates lines that don't sound good

Really cool for anyone generating voice at scale.

items.title: Jeeves CEO @thazhmon reveals why 60% of Argentina already uses stablecoins, while most Americans sti...
items.content:
Jeeves CEO @thazhmon reveals why 60% of Argentina already uses stablecoins, while most Americans still ask what they’re even for:

"If you're in the US, the first question is, 'Why would I use that?' And you don't need to. But outside the US, it gives protection against volatility."

"Imagine you get paid 500 Argentinian pesos, and the value of that a week from now is half. This is real. In Argentina, about 60% of the population use stablecoins."

"Previously the rails would require one to two correspondent banks in between, and would take one to two days. Now you do a classic stablecoin sandwich. You collect in one, you release the stablecoin, you pay on the other side. It takes one to two hours."

"We launched the stablecoin product in January, and we just crossed a billion and a half in annualized TPV. In eight to nine months, it's gone from zero to one and a half billion."
@jeeves_inc

items.content: On First Partial Transcript, MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming achieves a 2.5% WER at 0.12s after end of speech, ahead of Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 at 3.4% WER and 0.49s, and ahead of Muse Voice Transcribe and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime on accuracy, both at 3.6%, and slightly faster than both at 0.12s versus 0.13s. It is also more accurate than Cartesia Ink-2 with external endpoints at 4.0% WER and 0.07s, and AssemblyAI U3.5 Realtime Pro, whose Min Latency and Max Accuracy modes both achieve 4.0% WER. It is the lowest-error point on the First Partial Pareto frontier.

items.title: Jeeves CEO @thazhmon predicts stablecoin off-ramp fees will go from 1% to effectively zero, because ...
items.content:
Jeeves CEO @thazhmon predicts stablecoin off-ramp fees will go from 1% to effectively zero, because customers don’t care what rail moves the money as long as it arrives:

"I don't think you can win on fees, especially FX fees. Think about USDC or USDT off-ramping to USD. That used to be 1%, now it's five bps. Next is gonna be zero bps."

"What we do is we focus on the workflow automation. In Mexico, you put in your tax ID, we'll go download all your invoices, you hit a button, we'll fill out the payment information, and then you hit send. Really what they pay for is everything till the last step."

"It's like them saying, 'Can you send this using ACH?' Nobody says that. No one's like, 'Can you tell me which protocol you're using to send?' It's like, 'Is the money gonna show up? How much is it? Can I trust you?'"
@jeeves_inc

items.summary: Jeeves CEO Dileep Thazhmon predicts stablecoin off-ramp fees will compress from 1% to near zero, arguing companies win on workflow automation rather than payment rails, with an example of automated invoice-to-payment flows in Mexico.
items.reasoning: Coherent business thesis with concrete product examples from a founder, but fintech-focused rather than AI, and engagement is moderate.

"Building AI Agents for Finance: Build and deploy robust financial agentic systems with advanced reasoning, architectures, and Python"

items.content:
@johncrickett Right now, I consult for several companies. I help their engineering teams introduce AI into their workflows.

Each of these teams has become much more productive. Their software is better. They are delivering faster and more.

Focus has moved from "we need high-quality code so humans can maintain it" to "we need a strong process to validate what agents do".

I don't see how they will need "human coders" coming in the future to manually fix the code agents wrote.

items.title:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: SpaceX and NASA launched four astronauts to the ISS this morning.

• Crew Drago...
items.content:
SITUATION EXPLAINED: SpaceX and NASA launched four astronauts to the ISS this morning.

• Crew Dragon Grace on Falcon 9 booster B1101, out of Kennedy Space Center. Two Americans, a Canadian, and a Russian
• Falcon 9 is named after the Millennium Falcon and its nine Merlin engines. First flight 2010, first ISS trip 2012, first commercial crewed launch 2020
• Between the last Shuttle flight and that 2020 launch, the US had no way to put its own astronauts in space. NASA flew them to Baikonur in Kazakhstan to ride Soyuz
• The booster lands itself and gets reused. Older rockets were jettisoned and burned up, so you built a new one every flight
• Six months from now the crew undocks, fires a deorbit burn, and splashes down under parachutes
• Space is still one of the few areas where the US and Russia collaborate at all

@theojaffee: "You can see the rocket booster landing itself. Every time I see this, it's like it's not real."

“It looks like AI,” Maryam said.

“God has more GPUs than Elon,” I answered back.

First day without internet for quite a while and worth every minute.

Unfortunately Kancamagus Highway in New Hampshire only looks like this a couple of weeks out of the year. 

Very fortunate to be able to get my three boys together to experience it, along with other family.

Even the new iPhone 18 Pro Max doesn’t do it justice.
